body.statement: For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and any sequence \(d_n\ge2\), \(d_n/n\to0\) implies \(R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\to0\), while \(R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\to0\) implies \(d_n/[n\log(ed_n)]\to0\).
body.justification: The proposition records exactly what the current two-sided theory says about consistency without disguising the logarithmic gap.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 gives scalar consistency restrictions, not necessary and sufficient regions for a probability law under \(W_1\).
body.consumer: Study designers can distinguish a proved safe regime from a proved impossible regime for categorical heterogeneity reporting.
